hypothesis_test: Do measured tributary-flow changes (and retrospective gridded rain, if available) help predict Mankato streamflow relative to persistence?
limitations: USGS stage/discharge estimates can be provisional or revised; sensors are not independent draws.
Mankato flow includes upstream Minnesota basin, not just the two measured tributaries.
Hourly averages are computed retrospectively; gauge telemetry latency is not modeled.
Open-Meteo historical precipitation is gridded model/reanalysis context, not rain-gauge truth or guaranteed available at issue time.
Past-6h context is calculated using hours fully prior to target; report availability may lag.
Single watershed and short retrospective window; no flood thresholds or safety alert calibration.
Choosing a method on validation does not prove generalization across events, seasons or basins.
next_discriminating_question: Can we observe at least three independent rising-flow test hours before claiming flood/rise skill?

peer_diagnostic.JARVIS_to_MOTIF: Three gauges belong to coupled rivers. Shared weather, delayed reporting, and retrospective rainfall may create spurious causal-looking gains.
peer_diagnostic.MOTIF_to_JARVIS: Treat model selection on earlier validation as a held experiment; compare later physical test error before claiming a useful next action.
peer_diagnostic.self_diagnostic: This test may fail under a seasonal regime shift. The scorer can improve: use block-holdout by hydrologic event and fit a rainfall-free control.
